name: MITF (splash white)
summary: The first of two splash-white loci (with PAX3): white over the legs, belly and face, often a broad blaze and blue eyes, dominant and very variable in extent. UC Davis recognises six MITF splash variants - SW1, SW3, SW5, SW6, SW7 and SW8; SW1 is the widespread one and the rest are rare or confined to a family. SW9 is listed here only to mark it invalid: no published allele, test or paper was found for it, and the name may be a confusion with W9, a dominant white allele of KIT. No horse with two copies of SW3, SW5, SW6, SW7 or SW8 has been detected; UC Davis says such pairs may be lethal as embryos and advises against breeding two SW3 carriers. No outcome is published for a pair of two different variants. Splash is two genes, so a horse can carry a copy here and a copy at PAX3 and be whiter than either alone. Some splash-white horses, but not all, are deaf, and SW5 is reported with a raised risk. No genotype is confirmed by a source to cause deafness, so none is marked with it here.

alleles.name: Splash white 9 (invalid: no such published allele)

phenotypes.name: Splash white
phenotypes.description: One splash variant. Typically a broad blaze, white legs with a clean, sharply bounded edge, white on the belly and often blue eyes - but expression varies enormously: the same genotype can show no more than a star and a sock, or a great deal of white. No rule that one variant gives more white than another is established.

phenotypes.name: Bold splash white
phenotypes.description: Two copies of the same variant, where that pair is known alive. More white than one copy gives, and such a horse may be very extensively or entirely white.

phenotypes.name: Splash white, pair not documented
phenotypes.description: Two different MITF splash variants. No outcome is published for any such pair. More white than one variant gives is expected, and such a horse can be extensively white, but the exact outcome is variable and not characterised; no consistent appearance should be assumed.

phenotypes.name: Two copies, never detected
phenotypes.description: No horse with two copies of this variant has been detected. UC Davis says such homozygotes may be lethal as embryos; that is not established.

phenotypes.name: Pair with an invalid allele
phenotypes.description: A pair that includes SW9. No published allele, laboratory test or paper was found for an SW9; the name may be a confusion with W9, a dominant white allele of KIT. The allele is kept, marked invalid, so that it is not added again by mistake. No outcome can be given for it.
